metadata.title: The Running-Balance Bug Hiding in a Correct-Looking SQL Query
metadata.description: A real SQL correctness bug found and fixed in this book's Chapter 8 worked example: a date filter applied inside the running-balance CTE, before the cumulative SUM() OVER, silently truncating balance history for any account with pre-2026 activity. Fixed by moving the filter downstream to last_posting_per_month.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — open on the Claude UI, ask shown answered
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Supriya and this video is about the running-balance bug hiding in a correct-looking SQL query. It runs clean, and it's wrong for any account with a past.

props.command: claude "review this MySQL running-balance CTE for correctness before it ships"
output: wrong for any account with a past

beats.role_note: why care — stated before the CLI loop begins; SHOW-DON'T-TELL LAW: Manim, not a static card
beats.narration_text: In a bank's data warehouse, "what's this account's balance today" really means "sum every posting up to today." Get that running total right, and the report is trustworthy. Get one clause out of order, and the query still runs and still returns numbers, but they're wrong for any account with history before the reporting window. No error. No warning.
beats.visual_intent: a balance line accumulates smoothly across a 2025→2026 timeline; at the Jan 1 2026 boundary a red gate/cut mark appears with no alarm icon — the line keeps drawing past it uninterrupted, on-screen label 'no error thrown'

beats.role_note: the ordering rule — why the bug is possible at all
beats.narration_text: Here's the rule behind it. A window function runs after WHERE in the same query. So when the date filter sits in the same CTE as SUM() OVER, the sum only sees the rows that survived the filter. Everything posted before the window is gone before the total starts counting.
beats.visual_intent: split screen: LEFT — ledger rows flow into a filter funnel (rows before 2026 fade away) then into a SUM() OVER accumulator, landing on a small/wrong total, labeled WRONG in crimson; RIGHT — the same ledger rows flow whole into the accumulator first, landing on the true total, THEN a filter narrows to the reporting window, labeled RIGHT in teal. Brace + arrow annotations mark the order on each side.

beats.narration_text: So ask Claude to review a running-balance query before it ships: end-of-month balances for the first half of twenty twenty-six, built one CTE at a time.

props.command: claude "review this running-balance query: end-of-month balances for Jan–Jun 2026, one CTE at a time; flag anything wrong before it ships"

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL buggy CTE, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Here's the draft. Read the WHERE clause. It sits inside running, the same CTE as SUM() OVER, so the ledger is cut down to twenty twenty-six before the sum runs.

props.title: running_balance_buggy.mysql.sql (excerpt)
props.code:
WITH running AS (
  SELECT account_id, transaction_id, posted_at,
    SUM(amount) OVER (
      PARTITION BY account_id
      ORDER BY posted_at, transaction_id
      ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
    ) AS running_balance
  FROM transactions
  -- filters BEFORE the sum
  WHERE posted_at >= '2026-01-01'
    AND posted_at <  '2026-07-01'
),
last_posting_per_month AS (
  -- … ROW_NUMBER() … AS rn
  FROM running
),
-- rest of the query: same in both files

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot → Manim video — cycle 1, the wrong result
beats.narration_text: Run it on a Cascade Savings account that carried twelve thousand four hundred dollars into January. The query says January ended at minus three hundred. That's not a balance. It's the net change since January, and nothing warned you.
beats.visual_intent: animated result table for ACCT-50231: rows for Jan/Feb/Mar 2026 land one at a time showing -$300.00, -$150.00, -$225.00 in crimson; a pulsing crimson badge reads 'MISSING $12,400 OF HISTORY'

beats.narration_text: That's the bug. The fix moves one clause: take the date filter out of running, and put it on the next CTE, last posting per month.

props.command: claude "the date filter sits in the same CTE as SUM() OVER; move it to last_posting_per_month so the running total sees the full ledger"

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL fixed CTE (matches the book's shipped query)
beats.narration_text: Running now has no WHERE at all, so the sum sees the whole ledger. The same date filter sits one CTE later, after the balance is already right, and only narrows which months get reported. Nothing else changes.

props.title: running_balance_fixed.mysql.sql (excerpt)
props.code:
WITH running AS (
  SELECT account_id, transaction_id, posted_at,
    SUM(amount) OVER (
      PARTITION BY account_id
      ORDER BY posted_at, transaction_id
      ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
    ) AS running_balance
  -- no WHERE: the whole ledger
  FROM transactions
),
last_posting_per_month AS (
  -- … ROW_NUMBER() … AS rn
  FROM running
  -- moved here: after the sum
  WHERE posted_at >= '2026-01-01'
    AND posted_at <  '2026-07-01'
),
-- rest of the query: same in both files

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot → Manim video — cycle 2, the corrected result
beats.narration_text: Run it again. January ends at twelve thousand one hundred dollars: the real prior balance, minus the one January withdrawal. Nothing invented, nothing lost.
beats.visual_intent: mirrored version of B05's table: the crimson -$300.00/-$150.00/-$225.00 rows ghost, strike through, and fade; corrected teal rows land in their place: $12,100.00, $12,250.00, $12,175.00

beats.role_note: the lesson — one beat; SHOW-DON'T-TELL LAW: Manim, not a static card
beats.narration_text: So the bug was never the window function. It was a filter applied before the sum. Compute the running total over the whole ledger first, and narrow to your reporting window only after the balance is right.
beats.visual_intent: animated checklist, three lines landing with checkmarks: 'Compute the running total over the WHOLE ledger' / 'Filter to the reporting window only AFTER the sum' / 'A misplaced WHERE doesn't error — it quietly zeroes your history'; italic side-note beneath: 'Window functions run after WHERE inside their OWN query — not before a WHERE in an earlier CTE.'

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, viewer-addressed
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Try this: Check my running-balance query: is the date filter in the same CTE as SUM() OVER? If so, move it downstream and test it on an account with history before the window. If the answer is yes, that's your bug, and an account with older history is the test that proves the fix.
